- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in history (e.g., 73+), then corrects — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 73→65, 72→60), model often fails to adjust — apply downward correction in forecast horizon.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) followed by model overreaction — reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent peak.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, and sentiment is neutral or negative, apply downward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimation.
